The present claim petition was filed under Section 166 read with Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter "MV Act"), by the petitioner, Sh. Hansraj Yadav, regarding grievous injuries suffered by him in a road accident on 05.07.2015 involving a motor vehicle/truck bearing registration number HR 55 P 9031, which resulted in his permanent physical disability.

In view of the directions issued by the Hon'ble High Court, the rate of interest has been enhanced from 7.5% to 9% per annum.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of 1,50,37,561.60, along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition, that is, 24.09.2015, until realisation.

As on date, the petitioner is entitled to interest of 1,33,57,114/-, making the total amount payable,
inclusive of interest, 2,83,94,676/-.
Direction to Respondent No. 3/ Insurance Company 12.
Admittedly, the insurance company has already complied with original award dated 15.05.2023 and deposited the award amount along with interest.

As per the provisions of section 168(3) of MV Act, the enhanced award amount along with interest shall be deposited/transferred by respondent no.3/ Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd. in bank account of this Tribunal (Bank Account No. 42709452600 at State Bank of India, District Court Complex, Sector-10, Dwarka New Delhi, IFSC Code SBIN0011566 and MICR Code 110002483) by RTGS/NEFT/IMPS within 30 days of award under intimation to the Nazir of this Tribunal and with notice of deposit to the petitioner and his counsel.
MACT Account of the Petitioner 13.
The petitioner has his MACT account (SB A/c No. 40716003397) at State Bank of India, Branch District Court Complex, Sector-10, Dwarka, New Delhi (IFSC Code SBIN0011566).
Schedule of Disbursal.
14. The original award dated 15.05.2023 provides for a detailed scheme of disbursal of the award amount to the petitioner.
The petitioner has not expressed any dissatisfaction with that scheme.

Therefore, the award amount already deposited by the Insurance Company pursuant to said original award shall be governed by the scheme of disbursal/release provided in the paragraphs 30 and 31 of that award.
Learned counsel for petitioner submits that the petitioner is 60 years old and is in need of money.
In view of the same, 10% (ten percent) of the enhanced award amount along with interest is directed to be immediately released to the petitioner.

The remaining 90% (ninety percent) of the enhanced award amount along with interest be kept in the form of 5 fixed deposit receipts (FDRs) of equal amounts for period(s) of 1 year to 5 years in succession in the MACT account of the petitioner.
